full_judgment:
S. K. Sinha, J : These rules arise out of the same proceeding being G. R. Case No.159 of 1992 and accordingly these rules are taken up together for analogous hearing. This order would govern in both the rules. 

 2. Rule in Criminal Revision No.625 of 1999 was issued at the instance of Petitioners Dulal @ Dulal Talukder and Kamala Begum against the judgment and order dated 28.7.99 of the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Munshiganj in Criminal Appeal No. 29 of 1996 affirming that dated 13.7.96 of the learned Additional District Magistrate, Munshiganj in G. R. Case No.195 of 1992 convicting them along with other accused under section 366/34 of the Penal Code and sentencing the petitioner No.1 Dulal along with other accused to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 4 years with a fine of Tk.5,000/-, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 6 months more. Petitioner Kamala Begum, however. was sentenced to suffer simple imprisonment for 6 months with a fine of Tk.3000/-, in default, to suffer simple imprisonment for 2 months more. 

 3. Rule in Criminal Misc. Case No.8346 of 2002 arose at the instance of accused A.Rashid @ A.Rashid Talukder who unsuccessfully moved the learned Sessions Judge, Munshiganj for bail in Criminal Appeal No.24 of 2000 and thereafter obtained this rule. Petitioner A. Rashid was convicted under section 366 of the Penal Code and he was sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for 5 years with a fine of Tk.10,000/-, in default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 6 months more. A. Rashid preferred Criminal Appeal No.24 of 2000 before the learned Sessions Judge after the disposal of Criminal Appeal No. 29 of 1996. 

 4. Prosecution case is that the accused persons kidnapped the victim Rahima Begum (P.W.6) on 6.7.92 and over the said incident her father Md. Moslem Talukder (P.W.1) instituted Sreenagar Police Station Case No.11(7)92 and while the said case was pending in the Court of Additional District Magistrate, Munshiganj, the accused persons including the petitioners being armed with deadly weapons again kidnapped the victim Rahima Begum on 8.12.92 at about 5.30 P.M. Pursuant to the F.I.R. lodged by Md.Moslem Talukder with the Sreenagar Police Station, Sreenagar P.S. Case No.6 dated 8.12.92 was started. 

 5. The police after completion of investigation submitted charge sheet against the accused persons including the petitioners under sections 448/366A/34/109 of the Penal Code. The case record was eventually sent to the learned Additional District Magistrate, Munshiganj for trial. 

 8. The only point canvassed in these rules is that the trial of the case by the learned Additional District Magistrate was without jurisdiction and as such the conviction and sentence is liable to be quashed. It has been contended that the alleged occurrence took place on 8.12.92 when the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) ordinance, 1983 (ordinance No. XL/83) was in force and that the allegations as made in the. F.I.R. disclose an offence punishable under section 4 of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent ordinance), 1983 and therefore, the trial of the case by the learned Additional District Magistrate was without jurisdiction. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate has referred an unreported decision of a Division Bench of this Court in the case of Rashid @ A.Rashid Talukder Vs. The State, Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 3429 of 2000. 

 9. There is no dispute that the day on which the occurrence took place, the provisions of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) ordinance, 1983 was in force. The prosecution case is that the petitioners along with others abducted the victim Rashima Begum who was then a minor girl which gave rise to Sreenagar P.S. Case No.11(7)92 and that during the pendency of that case, the accused persons again kidnapped her on 8.12.92 at about 5.30 P.M. There is no allegation nor any evidence on record that the accused persons kidnapped the victim Rahima Begum with intent that she shall be employed or used for the purpose of prostitution or that she shall be used for immoral purpose or that she shall be compelled to marry with any person or that she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with any person. Section 4 of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) ordinance, 1983 provides the penalty for kidnapping or abduction of woman for unlawful or immoral purposes mentioned above which are totally absent in the facts of the given case. The Police after investigation of the case having found a prima-facie case of offences under sections 448/366A/34/109 of the Penal Code submitted charge sheet against the accused persons. The learned Magistrate also framed charge against the accused A. Rashid under section 366 of the Penal Code and as against other accused persons under section 366/34 of the Penal Code. 

 10. Therefore, we find that the trial of the petitioners under the provisions of the Penal Code was in accordance with law. Petitioners also did not raise this point in the trial Court as well as in the Court of Appeal below. Petitioners did not take any exception as regards the jurisdiction of the learned Additional District Magistrate in holding the trial of the case and they had surrendered to the jurisdiction of the learned Additional District Magistrate who had rightly tried them in accordance with law. Learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the offence as contained in 366 of the Penal Code merged with the offences disclosed in section 4 of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) ordinance, 1983. As pointed out above, the evidence on record does not disclose that the accused persons kidnapped Rahima Begum for any of the unlawful or immoral purposes mentioned in the said section. The evidence on record clearly discloses a simple case of abduction which is an offence punishable under section 365 of the Penal Code and the said offence has not been included as an offence, punishable under the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) ordinance 1983. Therefore, we find no substance in the submission of the learned Advocate. The decision referred by the learned Advocate is not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the case. 

 14. The accused petitioners had faced the charge of abduction of Rahima Begum. The prosecution has examined 6 witnesses in support of the abduction of the victim and the defence thoroughly cross examined them. The defence also examined one witness in dis-proof of the charge. The accused petitioners were furnished with all necessary informations and they also defended to the accusations brought against them. It is not a case that no formal charge was framed against the accused persons for which, they were prejudiced in taking their defence. However, we find that there is mere an error or omission in the charge and that the accused persons did not raise any objection at an earlier stage in the proceedings. We are therefore, of the view that whatever the error it is not to be regarded as fatal and the accused persons are not prejudiced by reason of such error in the charge.
